description: Ash is a tough, springy, ring-porous hardwood with bold grain, prized for tool handles, bats, oars and steam-bent parts as well as furniture and joinery. White ash (Fraxinus americana) and European ash (Fraxinus excelsior) are the main woodworking species.

hazards.summary: Occupational asthma and rhinitis from ash dust have been confirmed by inhalation challenge in separate cases involving European ash and white ash, and in a third case with a positive skin test to ash wood.
UK HSE lists reduced lung function among the reported effects of ash dust.
A case of allergic contact dermatitis to white ash has been described in a woodworker. The testing method was not confirmed from the available abstract.
IARC classifies all wood dust as carcinogenic to humans, mainly linked to cancer of the nasal cavity and sinuses after long, heavy exposure. This applies to this wood like any other.

exposure_limits.note: 8-hour TWA; ACGIH value as restated by OSHA.

related_species_note: Respiratory cases involve European ash (Fraxinus excelsior) and white ash (Fraxinus americana); the Polish case does not name the species. Ash pollen allergy is distinct from wood dust allergy. Mountain ash (Sorbus) and prickly ash are not true ashes.
image_prompt: Photorealistic studio photograph of a freshly planed white ash (Fraxinus americana) board, shot at a low three-quarter angle so the face grain fills most of the frame. Wide band of creamy off-white to very pale tan sapwood with light greyish-brown to light brown heartwood. Bold, straight, ring-porous grain with clearly visible large earlywood pores forming open lines and cathedral arches on the flatsawn face, coarse but even texture, moderate natural luster. Soft diffused daylight from upper left, gentle falloff, neutral warm-grey seamless background, shallow depth of field with the near edge tack-sharp. No text, no logos, no hands, no tools, no finish or varnish, natural unfinished wood. Wide 1200x630 composition (1.91:1) with the board centered and margin on both sides for cropping.
image_alt: Planed board of white ash with creamy pale wood and bold, open, straight grain.
notes_internal: FernandezRivas-1997 page range confirmed as 196-199. Scheman-1999 kept at level 3 because test method not readable. Szmidt-1994 exposure was non-occupational. White ash name (Fraxinus americana L.) returned two candidates on WFO matching (L. vs Marshall); genus is verified.
